summary: Qualify each immutable release candidate on all supported TypeORM databases and a pinned real Operaton browser journey before publication.

notes: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and Spanner execute as independent candidate shards, followed by one aggregate schema-equivalence check.

security: The candidate source validator remains read-only and proves the exact release-only delta before any workflow with package write authority runs.
Database credentials and the Operaton fixture remain isolated to disposable candidate jobs.
documentation: Candidate receipts record the five-database aggregate and pinned Operaton browser result as distinct release evidence.
knownLimitations: A single database shard or the supported Operaton journey being skipped, missing, or failed blocks candidate readiness.
rollback: Revert candidate qualification changes and retain the previous full local readiness workflow; do not publish a candidate whose new receipt is incomplete.
validation: The physical database matrix passes all five supported adapters with one schema fingerprint.
The authenticated Operaton 2.1.0 browser journey verifies health, version persistence, process start, completed overview, detail navigation, final variables, BPMN rendering, and clean diagnostics.
Workflow contracts verify every shard and aggregate is a non-skippable candidate dependency.
